title: The amber hatch, no longer a box
question: Does the amber now read as ground that fed them, rather than as blocks dropped on the scene -- and can you follow the ants' road through it?
context_md:
You said of this view: ***"the amber hatch it bad"***, and on the other bed ***"why is the amber hatch drop like a huge box?"***

Rendering the two channels apart said why in one frame, and it was not subtle. **The amber was being painted on the sky.** Every patch of ground a colony feeds off sits in the surface band; the wash covered a square eight cells on a side around it, and seven of those eight rows are open air. So the shape you were seeing was the grid, not the ground -- a hard-edged block with a dead straight top edge hanging over the terrain.

It now marks only the **exposed face of the ground**, so its outline is the land. Same run, same seed, same frames; the only difference is where the amber is allowed to fall.

- **amber** -- ground this colony has taken food out of, brighter the more it gave up, fading over about a minute of play
- **red-orange** -- an ant walked here **carrying**
- **blue** -- an ant walked here with nothing

**The second thing this bought, and it is the bigger one:** the seven rows it stops painting were the rows sitting on top of the road. In A the road is underneath the hatch and in nearly the same colour. In B you can see it.

**What I am unsure of and would rather you judged:** whether the amber has now gone too quiet to say anything. It covers about a fifth of the pixels it used to.

items.label: A -- as you saw it
items.caption: the wash covers its whole tile, air included

items.label: B -- clipped to the ground
items.caption: the same marks, drawn only where there is ground to mark
